facts.fact: The World Bank's Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project has an activity to provide last-mile broadband access to selected public institutions, named as ministries, departments and agencies, local government offices, hospitals and health clinics, and schools, in Freetown and in secondary cities that have no broadband; its feasibility study had been started by the implementation support mission of April 2025.

The World Bank counts 50 public institutions connected to broadband internet under the project at 28 July 2025, unchanged from 13 January 2025, against a target of 300 by June 2027; the count covers ministries, local government offices, health facilities and schools together and gives no figure for local government offices.

The last-mile connectivity activity sits in Component 1 of the Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project, costed at USD 21.3 million of a USD 50 million World Bank IDA grant (IDA-E1130), of which 21.24 per cent was disbursed at 24 August 2025; no domestic budget line is stated.

systems.owner: Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project (World Bank P177077), through its project coordination unit
systems.tiers: selected public institutions including local government offices, at central and local levels in Freetown and in secondary cities without broadband

systems.system: Government-wide area network (GWAN) and Government-local area network (GLAN)
systems.tiers: ministries, departments and agencies; procurement started by April 2025; 0 of a target 300 institutions benefiting from improved government networks at 28 July 2025

note: The report names local government offices only inside a list of the kinds of institution the activity is to reach; it does not say that any council office has been connected.
